## Natural history notes

A small, stout frog characterized by a narrow pointed snout, smooth skin, short legs, and a rounded body that is usually gray, brown, or reddish-brown with variable mottling. In Florida, the Eastern Narrow-mouthed Toad is found in pine flatwoods, hammocks, sandy uplands, wetlands, gardens, yards, and areas with leaf litter, logs, or loose soil where it can hide. It feeds heavily on ants and termites, emerging most often after rains and breeding in shallow temporary pools, ditches, and flooded depressions where males give a high, nasal, sheep-like call.
